findings.reason: Operations.js:307 and :312 are arrow functions inside the module-level reverseFactory, so `this` at line 320 is undefined, not reversedSequence. Any reverse iteration over a non-keyed reversed sequence (e.g. Seq([1,2]).reverse().map(x=>x).reverse().entries().next()) now throws a TypeError. The old `reversedSequence.size` and the warning comment explaining it were removed in the diff.
findings.claim: Replacing reversedSequence.size with this.size in the arrow-function __iterator makes reverse iteration of a reversed indexed sequence throw a TypeError.
findings.evidence: `reversedSequence.__iterator = (type, reverse) => { ... return new Iterator(() => { ... useKeys ? entry[0] : reverse ? this.size - ++i : i++ ...` (lines 307-323). Both enclosing functions are arrows defined at the top level of an ES module, so `this` is `undefined` there and reading `this.size` throws "Cannot read properties of undefined". The diff also deletes the comment that warned about exactly this: "`__iterator` is an arrow function, so `this` is not the reversed sequence here — read `reversedSequence.size` explicitly." The sibling `__iterate` at line 298 is a regular `function`, which is why `this.size` works at line 303 and not at 320. How it fails: any non-keyed reversed sequence iterated in reverse through an iterator hits the `reverse` branch. One example is `Seq([1,2,3]).reverse().map(x => x).reverse().values()`: the outer reverseFactory calls `mapped.__iterator(ITERATE_ENTRIES, true)`, which calls `reversed.__iterator(..., true)`. Existing tests such as `__tests__/KeyedSeq.ts:133` (`seq.reverse().toKeyedSeq().skip(10).take(5).reverse()`) exercise reverse iteration over a reversed sequence. Nothing else in the change computes this index, so no other code takes over the job the removed line did.

findings.reason: diff.patch touches only src/Operations.js and adds no test pinning the indices from the reverse __iterator path. I lowered severity to low because a missing test is a coverage gap, not a defect in its own right; the defect itself is the C1/X1 item.
findings.claim: No test covers the backward __iterator path of a reversed indexed sequence.
findings.evidence: diff.patch changes only `src/Operations.js` and adds or changes no test. The only change is replacing `reversedSequence.size` with `this.size` on the `__iterator` reverse path, and no test in the diff pins the indices that path yields.
